card: Updates the libmultiprocess subtree to add non-Unix platform support and fix several concurrency bugs, including an IPC disconnect data race found by Antithesis, a use-after-free during client connection, and a file descriptor leak during concurrent process spawning. It also adds serialization features required by multiprocess PRs #10102 and #29409, enables Windows build support needed by #32387, and suppresses C++23 lambda attribute compiler warnings in C++20 builds. This work benefits users and developers testing experimental multiprocess nodes by fixing race conditions and unblocking downstream multiprocess work.
evidence: PR description notes it fixes "a data race between IPC calls running on worker threads and disconnects, found by Antithesis" (libmultiprocess #349)
PR description notes it fixes "a use-after-free when a socket disconnects before ConnectStream connects, and leaks and hangs when a client construct() call throws" (libmultiprocess #298)
PR description documents serialization extensions specifically required by open PRs #10102 and #29409, and Windows capnp path detection needed by #32387
problem: Experimental multiprocess support lacks non-Unix platform capability, suffers from IPC disconnection races and lifetime bugs (including a use-after-free and thread-safety issues during process spawning), and lacks serialization features needed by subsequent multiprocess pull requests.

risk.why: Bugs would only affect experimental multiprocess builds and would not impact monolithic production binaries or consensus validation.

scope_notes: Subtree update of `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` (+1645/-544) with one additional build configuration commit in Bitcoin Core.
summary: Updates the `src/ipc/libmultiprocess` subtree to add non-Unix platform support, fix several concurrency and lifetime bugs, and add serialization features. Also updates build warning flags to suppress C++23 lambda attribute warnings in C++20 builds caused by attributes introduced in the subtree.
